# Files at or past 600 lines, frozen as a ratchet.
# Regenerate with: scripts/check-file-size.sh --update
#
# This file records existing debt so CI can block *growth* without
# blocking every edit to a file that was already too big. Numbers
# here should only ever go down. Adding a row is not a normal part
# of landing a change — it means a new file crossed the line, and
# the split should happen instead.
#
# Three rows have been raised on purpose. They are named in the script
# that writes this header, not in the file, because --update rewrites
# the file from scratch and would drop a note added by hand:
#
#   frontend-shared/src/api/types.ts  717 -> 750  (issue 275)
#                                     674 -> 676  (issue 488)
#     The hand-written Rust<->TS wire mirror. It grows when the wire
#     grows; splitting it to save 20 lines would refactor every
#     client's type contract. The pins in outl-tauri-shared/tests/
#     are what keep it honest, not its length.
#     The second raise is two lines: PasteReply moved to api/paste.ts
#     to sit with the two wrappers that return it, and what stayed
#     behind is the re-export that keeps the import path unchanged.
#     The same move took commands.ts down by 41 lines.
#     The third raise is 34 lines for DroppedEdit plus the PageView
#     field that carries it (issue 473): a keystroke whose target block
#     had left the tree. It is the registered reason above, verbatim -
#     the wire grew, so the mirror grew. The pin is wire_types.rs's
#     dropped_edit_matches_its_interface.
#                                     707 -> 711  (issue 572)
#     The fourth raise is four lines, and three of them are the comment
#     saying where the type went: RemindFields is declared in
#     commands-reminders.ts beside parseRemindRule / formatRemindRule,
#     the arrangement PasteReply already has, so what is left here is
#     the re-export that keeps the import path one. The pin is
#     wire_types.rs's remind_fields_match_their_interface, and
#     commands-reminders.ts joined ts_parser::MIRROR_FILES so the
#     declaration is read rather than merely moved out of sight.
#
#   outl-desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs  616 -> 618  (issue 572)
#     Two lines: the two reminder-authoring commands in the
#     invoke_handler list (their names join an existing import line).
#     The file is a registration list, and the rule it registers under
#     is that a client takes a whole command module or declares the gap
#     - so a shared module gaining two commands grows both clients by
#     the same two lines, by design. Splitting the handler list to
#     avoid that would put half a registration in another file, which
#     is the state command_parity.rs exists to catch.
#
#   frontend-shared/src/api/commands.ts  859 -> 861  (issue 572)
#     Two names in the existing re-export block: parseRemindRule and
#     formatRemindRule, the pair that reads and writes a remind:: rule
#     for the mobile picker that replaced a window.prompt. The bodies
#     are in commands-reminders.ts, where every other reminder wrapper
#     already lives; these two lines are what keeps
#     @outl/shared/api/commands the single import path, which is the
#     reason the split file exists at all.
#     (No backticks in this block — the header is written through an
#     unquoted heredoc, so one becomes a command substitution and the
#     sentence silently loses the word.)
#
#   outl-tui/src/state.rs  976 -> 983  (issue 275)
#     One memo field. The nested-pages rows cost two full-workspace
#     node scans and the TUI render path runs every frame, so
#     uncached that was a per-frame cost on a 64k-node workspace.
#
#   outl-actions/src/sync.rs  673 -> 683
#     A stop flag for FileSyncTransport. Its polling thread owned the
#     Sender it was handed, so dropping the Receiver never ended it on
#     a quiet workspace. The desktop is who that cost: a workspace swap
#     replaces the transport, so every swap left a two-second poller
#     running for the life of the process, and shutdown was a no-op
#     comment claiming otherwise. The ten lines are the field, the
#     clone into the thread, the per-tick check and the store.
#     Splitting a 673-line file to land a leak fix is the larger
#     change, not the smaller one.
#
#     (No backticks in this block: the heredoc below is deliberately
#     unquoted so it can interpolate THRESHOLD, which means a backtick
#     here runs as a command and silently empties the words around it.)
#
#   outl-actions/src/page.rs  682 -> 689  (issue 473)
#     The dispatch branch that routes a reopened-by-slug page out of the
#     trash: open_or_create already computes the deterministic root id
#     at this point, so checking whether it is trashed and handing off
#     to the revive helper is seven lines in the one place that already
#     decides what a slug resolves to. The revival logic itself (and its
#     tests) is a sibling module, same split as the existing page_merge
#     and page_repair siblings, so page.rs only pays for the call site.
#
#   outl-mobile/src/components/Journal.tsx  1798 -> 1804  (issue 16)
#     Six lines to wire a ((blk-...)) ref resolver: one import, two
#     comment lines, the const, the resolve call in applyView, and the
#     prop on BlockRow. The logic is not here - Journal.embeds.ts is 110
#     lines and its test 196, and the module owns the signal too, so the
#     component holds no state for this feature. Mobile printed raw
#     handles on every ref because this client never called
#     resolveEmbeds; the backend and the renderer both already had it.
#     What is left in Journal.tsx is a state and effects question (edit
#     lifecycle, sync signals, native bridges, the sheet stack), which
#     outl-mobile/CLAUDE.md records as wanting its own plan - phases 1-3
#     of issue 265 already took the movable half. Extracting more of it
#     to pay for six lines is the larger change, and the silent failure
#     it risks is a destructured prop frozen at first render.
#
# None of these arguments generalises. A further raise makes its own case.
